name: ELS
description: The Endoluminal Surgical (ELS) System is an investigational flexible teleoperated robotic platform developed by EndoQuest Robotics (formerly ColubrisMX) for natural-orifice gastrointestinal procedures—such as colorectal and upper-GI endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), full-thickness resection, and endoluminal suturing—as well as single-incision transumbilical surgery. The architecture comprises a mobile bedside patient cart (EndoDrive actuation unit) that positions a steerable flexible overtube delivering an articulating HD videoscope, working channels for insufflation, irrigation, and suction, and two 7-degree-of-freedom flexible robotic instruments (3.7–6 mm graspers, scissors, electrosurgical knives, and needle drivers) to establish bimanual triangulation and countertraction inside the GI lumen. The open physician console pairs an HD display and mode-switching foot pedals with dual OEM [Force Dimension lambda.7](/robot/force_dimension_lambda) 7-DOF haptic master interfaces (succeeding the [Force Dimension omega.7](/robot/force_dimension_omega) controllers used in the earlier ColubrisMX ELS prototype). Enrolled in the US FDA Safer Technologies Program (STeP), the system received FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) approval in December 2024 and completed patient enrollment across 50 colorectal ESD procedures in the multicenter PARADIGM pivotal trial in 2026 toward an FDA De Novo submission.
